correctness_confidence.basis: The estimates transfer through the two Gram products. The local return comparison counts the first index in a dyadic noise band and includes multiplicities. For the three-level construction the shell, companion shell and off-shell transitions each carry a strictly positive exponential margin after fixing the parameters in order. No formal proof or independent audit of the full chain of estimates is supplied.

rigor.basis: The argument separates rarity exponents, stationary masses, conditional measures and dimension dependence. The endpoint small-support gain uses the support hypothesis and time of Theorem 7 of Polyanskiy and Samorodnitsky. Some limiting and normalization steps require consulting earlier sections and the cited shell construction.

novelty.basis: Earlier programme work already gives a matched shell trap. The present claim is stronger in a different respect: two exact stationary values have a uniform cubic gap, while three exact values permit exponentially slow escape. The matched extension has approximate levels. I did not establish exhaustive priority.

significance.basis: The distinction between two and three stationary levels, the local criterion for ordered spectral recovery and the floor-free quotient criterion answer specific questions for finite Boolean half-noise. The critical exponent for arbitrary matched laws remains open.

reproducibility.basis: Two source checkouts on one dedicated Colab runtime produced identical bytes. I inspected the 18 page renderings and compared the equations with the pinned TeX input. Reproduction verifies typesetting. The existence examples are analytic and their asymptotic constants have not undergone independent numerical or formal verification.

summary: This 18-page supplement merits circulation as a working paper. Its strongest comparison identifies the minimum number of distinct stationary density values that can yield exponentially slow relaxation under a fixed floor and a uniform cubic bound. Exact one-coordinate matching is retained in the three-level example. The higher-order matched construction is only exponentially close to three levels, as correctly stated. I checked the exponents in the coarea, sparse-input and fractional-packing arguments and the ordering used in the local-return spectral comparison. As a participant in the same research chat I had access to the source and prior programme context. This is a first assessment of the identified PDF, without peer review or a claim of independent discovery.
strengths: Sections 4 and 6 prove complementary statements concerning the number of values of the stationary density itself. A cubic norm bound forces escape for every subset of the unique spike; the three-level construction explicitly controls atypical transitions from the rarer shell.

Section 2 bounds the ordered spectral error above and below by the norm of a killed operator on a specified tail, uses a doubled Hilbert space to count multiplicities, and relates that norm to actual one-step return probabilities.

The quotient estimate spends the entire ordinary noise time on the potential after obtaining a dimension-uniform positive-measure level set. With t=2 its strict condition is exactly p>15/7. Its example at t=5/2 separates it from the four-family sufficient estimate.
weaknesses: The supplement is dense. A short table of which results require a floor, matching or a stationary moment would make the distinctions easier to use. Several proof inputs are accessible only by hyperlinks rather than a consolidated bibliography.

The quantitative sufficient and obstructed logarithmic mass ratios leave an interval, and the examples do not identify a sharp general moment threshold. The auxiliary interpolation imports the earlier shell result.
potential_errors: On page 11, 'The ordinary second eigenvalue moves' should say the second eigenvalue of the perturbed chain. The ordinary comparator is fixed at 1/2; the displayed eigenvalues and the order-of-displacement argument use the correct interpretation.

The PDF uses historical present-tense statements about pending assessment. They describe its preparation before this external-to-the-PDF report; the version record should supply the actual assessment date.
